paragraphs.title: David’s Victories and the Submission of Neighboring Peoples

easy.explanation: The passage says that David smote the Philistines and subdued them.
easy.q: Whom did David smite at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: David took Gath and her towns out of the hand of the Philistines.
easy.q: What city and its towns did David take from the Philistines?

easy.explanation: After David smote Moab, the Moabites became his servants and brought gifts.
easy.q: Which people became David’s servants and brought gifts?

answers: He smote Moab, and then the Philistines
He smote the Philistines, and then Moab
He smote Edom, and then Moab
medium.explanation: The passage first describes David’s victory over the Philistines and then his defeat of Moab.
medium.q: What was the correct order of David’s actions?

answers: The Moabites paid tribute to David
The Moabites guarded the city gates
medium.explanation: The phrase shows that the Moabites were subject to David and gave him tribute.
medium.q: What does the phrase “brought gifts” indicate in this context?

answers: David lost control of the region
David expanded his control over Philistine territory
David made a peace treaty with the Philistines
medium.explanation: Taking Gath and its towns shows that David expanded his rule over Philistine territory.
medium.q: What can be inferred from David taking Gath and her towns?

answers: The Moabites became David’s servants and brought gifts
challenge.explanation: Becoming servants shows submission, while bringing gifts shows the payment of tribute.
challenge.q: Which detail shows both military victory and political submission by Moab?

answers: The Philistines were brought under David’s control
The Philistines sent gifts to Hamath
challenge.explanation: To subdue them means that David brought the Philistines under his authority.
challenge.q: What does the statement that David “subdued” the Philistines imply?

answers: Both describe David’s growing power over neighboring peoples
Both describe the appointment of David’s officers
Both describe the dedication of spoils to the LORD
challenge.explanation: Both verses portray David defeating neighboring peoples and establishing their submission.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the two verses?

paragraphs.title: The Campaign against Hadarezer and Aram

easy.explanation: David smote Hadarezer king of Zobah.
easy.q: Whom did David smite as he went to establish his dominion by the river Euphrates?

easy.explanation: David houghed the chariot horses but reserved an hundred chariots.
easy.q: How many chariots did David reserve after destroying the rest of the chariot force?

easy.explanation: The Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadarezer.
easy.q: Which army came to help Hadarezer?

answers: He took all of it to Jerusalem
He destroyed most of it and reserved an hundred chariots
He gave it to the king of Hamath
medium.explanation: David houghed the chariot horses and kept only an hundred chariots.
medium.q: What did David do to the chariot force of Hadarezer?

answers: The Syrians became David’s servants and brought gifts
The Syrians made David their king
medium.explanation: David put garrisons in Syria-damascus, and the Syrians became his servants and brought gifts.
medium.q: What was the result of David’s victory over the Syrians of Damascus?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to gold shields belonging to the servants of Hadarezer.
medium.q: In the KJV context, what were the “shields of gold”?

answers: It was a confrontation with a significant military force
It was only a religious ceremony
Hadarezer ruled only a small village
challenge.explanation: The many chariots, horsemen, and footmen indicate a large and powerful army.
challenge.q: What does the large number of soldiers and chariots reveal about the campaign against Hadarezer?

answers: The spoils were taken from the defeated forces and brought to David’s capital
The spoils were sent to David before the war
The spoils were returned to Hadarezer
challenge.explanation: After the victory, David took the gold shields and brought them to Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What is the connection between David’s victory and bringing the spoils to Jerusalem?

answers: Hadarezer was defeated, the Syrians came to help, and they were also defeated
The Syrians were defeated, and then David appointed Hadarezer
David received spoils, and then first went against Hadarezer
challenge.explanation: David first defeated Hadarezer, then defeated the Syrians who came to help him, and afterward took spoils.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the development of the campaign?

paragraphs.title: David’s Relations with Hamath and the Dedication of Spoils

easy.explanation: Tou king of Hamath heard how David had smitten Hadarezer’s host.
easy.q: Who heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadarezer?

easy.explanation: Tou sent Hadoram his son to king David.
easy.q: Whom did Tou send to David?

easy.explanation: David dedicated the vessels and other spoils unto the LORD.
easy.q: To whom did David dedicate the gold, silver, and brass?

answers: To enquire of David’s welfare and congratulate him
medium.explanation: Hadoram came to ask about David’s welfare and congratulate him on his victory.
medium.q: Why did Tou send Hadoram to David?

answers: Edom, Moab, Ammon, the Philistines, and Amalek
medium.explanation: The passage lists Edom, Moab, the children of Ammon, the Philistines, and Amalek.
medium.q: From which nations did David bring some of the silver and gold that he dedicated?

answers: To honor David and express approval of his victory
To appoint David as a military officer
medium.explanation: Hadoram came to honor David because he had defeated Hadarezer.
medium.q: What does “to congratulate him” mean in this context?

answers: David’s victory affected his diplomatic relations with Hamath
Hamath had been defeated in battle by David
Tou became David’s servant and tribute-payer
challenge.explanation: Tou’s respectful message and gifts show that the victory influenced relations between Hamath and David.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the gifts sent after David’s victory over Hadarezer?

answers: They were set apart for God rather than kept merely as private wealth
They were returned to all the nations
They were used to pay the Syrians
challenge.explanation: David dedicated the valuable objects and other spoils unto the LORD.
challenge.q: What does dedicating the spoils unto the LORD reveal about their use?

answers: Solomon used it to make the brasen sea, the pillars, and vessels of brass
Solomon returned the brass to Tou
Solomon used it to conquer Hamath
challenge.explanation: The brass from Hadarezer’s cities was later used by Solomon for temple furnishings.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between the brass taken and Solomon?

easy.explanation: The passage says that David reigned over all Israel.
David executed judgment and justice among all his people.
easy.q: What did David execute among all his people?

easy.explanation: Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the host.

medium.explanation: Jehoshaphat is identified as the recorder.
medium.q: What position did Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud hold?

answers: Zadok the son of Ahitub and Abimelech the son of Abiathar
medium.explanation: Zadok and Abimelech were named as the priests.
medium.q: Who were the priests mentioned in the passage?

answers: They helped administer the army, government, worship, and royal court
They were all kings of neighboring nations
They were all captives from Syria
medium.explanation: The verses list military, administrative, priestly, scribal, and royal positions.
medium.q: How were the listed officials connected with David’s kingdom?

answers: David’s rule included both righteous values and an organized system of government
Judgment and justice were carried out only by David’s army
The list of officials removed David from authority
challenge.explanation: The passage presents David as a just ruler and then describes the officials who supported his kingdom.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between judgment and justice and the list of officials?

answers: Joab was over the host and Jehoshaphat was recorder
Zadok and Abimelech served as priests
The sons of David were chief about the king
challenge.explanation: Joab represents military leadership, while Jehoshaphat held an administrative position.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the royal administration included both military and governmental roles?

answers: They were part of the king’s court and governing household
They served as priests in Syria
challenge.explanation: The phrase places David’s sons among the leading members of his royal court.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the statement that David’s sons were “chief about the king”?
